correctness.rationale: The exact two-box ODE has generator [[-k-ell1,k],[k,-k-ell2]] and initial (1,0). Writing m=(ell1+ell2)/2, delta=(ell1-ell2)/2 gives x2(T;k)=exp(-(k+m)T)k*sinh(T sqrt(k²+delta²))/sqrt(k²+delta²) by a 2x2 matrix exponential. For dimensionless y=kT, r=(Tdelta)², the log derivative of y exp(-y)sinh(sqrt(y²+r))/sqrt(y²+r) is D=r/[y(y²+r)]+y/z*coth(z)-1. When r>0, D is positive near zero and negative for large y. Substitution of its critical equation yields D_y|D=0=-r(y²-3y+3)/(y²(y²+r))<0, so all crossings are strictly downward and the root is unique and globally optimal. D(1,r)>0 proves y*>1. The sign D_r<0 follows from positive hyperbolic series H(z)=z sinh z cosh z+z²-2sinh²z=sum_{n>=3}[(n-2)2^(2n-1)/(2n)!]z^(2n); hence the root strictly decreases as r increases. Limits r down to0 and up to infinity and peak above perfect-mixing value follow. At r=0 response (1-exp(-2y))/2 is monotone with no finite optimum. Swapping losses leaves x2 invariant. Independent symbolic curvature identity and numerical roots confirm, not replace, all-r proof.

The Comp2Exchange no-loss model is an even simpler known specialization. Historical transport literature may have an equivalent optimization under another name; inaccessible full 1984/2000 texts are explicitly retained as risks.
